diagnostic_evidence.quote: From the convergence plots, it is evident that the estimates presented in Section~\ref{sec:error_analysis} are confirmed by all the numerical tests

issues.failure_explanation: The method and its error analysis assume homogeneous Dirichlet boundary conditions. Test 2 uses an exact solution with nonzero velocity on the top boundary. Since the discrete velocity space enforces zero boundary conditions, the discrete solution cannot approximate this exact solution near the boundary without a lifting or modification of the method. The claim that Test 2 confirms the theoretical estimates is therefore unsupported.

failure_location.quote: The velocity in Test~1 has homogeneous Dirichlet boundary conditions on the entire $\partial\Omega$, whereas the velocity in Test~2 has nonzero Dirichlet boundary conditions on the top edge of the domain.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Either modify Test 2 to have homogeneous Dirichlet boundary conditions, or introduce and describe a lifting to handle nonzero boundary data and adjust the discrete problem accordingly.
issues.overall_effect: The numerical validation of the theoretical estimates is invalid for Test 2. The paper's claim that all numerical tests confirm the theory is false.
issues.title: Numerical Test 2 violates homogeneous Dirichlet boundary condition assumption
issues.why_classification: The theoretical results are unaffected, but a numerical test is invalid, requiring a contained fix (change test or add lifting).
